title: Asia stocks hold up as Nvidia leadership crisis clouds AI trade
full_text:
Investing.com -- Asian stocks held modest gains on Thursday as investors weighed resilient technology shares against fresh uncertainty over Nvidia’s leadership, after reports that its board was discussing the future of Chief Executive Jensen Huang.
The MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose 0.3%, led by technology shares, even as Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.86% and S&P 500 futures lost 0.35% in Asian trade.
Wall Street had rallied on Wednesday, with the Nasdaq 100 jumping 2.3% and the S&P 500 gaining 1.3%, leaving the latter close to recovering its losses since last week’s U.S. midterm elections.
The rally reflected renewed confidence in AI demand. CoreWeave shares surged 25% after the cloud-computing provider raised its annual outlook, OpenAI reported quarterly revenue of $10 billion and Anthropic’s planned initial public offering was said to be multiple times oversubscribed. Nvidia’s after-hours slump has since unsettled investors.
Nvidia turmoil puts AI leadership risk back in focus
Nvidia shares fell more than 8% in after-hours trading, having dropped as much as 10%, on reports that the board was weighing whether to remove Huang.
Directors were reported to be meeting on Wednesday to discuss his future, while the company has been working with an outside firm to identify potential successors and considering an interim chief executive.
The reports follow allegations of two extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman reportedly suspected by U.S. authorities of links to Chinese intelligence.
The New York Times also reported that Huang had a relationship with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife but gave no details. Nvidia’s board has opened an investigation and said it had no reason to believe company secrets or U.S. national security were compromised.
The uncertainty matters because Nvidia sits at the centre of the AI investment boom and Huang has been closely identified with its rise. A leadership vacuum could unsettle confidence in the chipmaker and wider AI supply chain, even as demand for computing capacity remains strong.
Asian markets diverge as investors reassess risk
Japan’s Nikkei 225 edged up 0.1% and TOPIX gained 0.6%, while South Korea’s KOSPI slipped 0.2%.
Taiwan shares rose 0.5% in earlier trading. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 1%, weighing on the Asia ex-Japan gauge, which was down 0.1% in early trade. Mainland China was steadier, with the CSI 300 up 0.1% and Shanghai Composite gaining 0.2%.
Elsewhere, Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.3%, New Zealand’s NZX 50 rose 0.6% and Singapore’s Straits Times Index was little changed.
India’s Nifty 50 Futures advanced 0.7%. Indonesia’s Jakarta Composite climbed 1.3%, while the Philippines’ PSEi fell 1.1%, Malaysia’s KLCI lost 0.6% and Thailand’s SET was flat. Nikkei futures fell 1.1%.
Oil drifted toward a two-month low as Middle East production increased and hostilities between Iran and the United States remained muted. The dollar held near an 18-month high, with markets fully pricing a 25-basis-point Fed rate increase next month and assigning a smaller chance to a 50-basis-point move.
Fed funds futures showed an 87.3% probability of a quarter-point increase at the December 9 meeting, against 12.7% for a half-point hike.

title: U.S. finalizing rule to block China’s remote AI chip access- The Information
full_text:
Investing.com-- The Commerce Department is preparing to finalize a rule that will prevent Chinese artificial intelligence companies from remotely accessing advanced AI chips through data centers located in other countries, The Information reported on Wednesday, citing two people familiar with the matter.
The rule could be announced this month and will expand current semiconductor-related controls from the department’s Bureau of Industry and Security. The expanded controls will apply to seven additional countries, including Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, the report said.

The measure aims to prevent remote access and chip smuggling into China, and comes amid a growing row over Nvidia’s potential links to China after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a suspected Beijing spy.
Chinese internet giants including Tencent, Alibaba, and Bytedance have all signed offshore data center agreements granting them access to Nvidia’s top chips to train their artificial intelligence models. But said deals are facing increasing scrutiny both abroad and home, especially as Beijing pushes for the use of more domestic chips.
The Commerce Department is consulting with other government agencies on the rule before it can be finalized, the Information reported.
Earlier on Wednesday, Axios reported that U.S. President Donald Trump had pushed for tighter export controls against China to prevent illegal chip smuggling to the country. But Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick was a major opponent to the measure.

title: Nvidia worth 25% less without Jensen Huang as CEO, Yorkville Ives says
full_text:
Investing.com-- Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) could lose a quarter of its valuation if Chief Executive Jensen Huang leaves the chipmaker, as mounting reports about his personal conduct and the possibility of a boardroom shake-up threaten to unsettle investors, brokerage Yorkville Ives said.
Analysts led by Dan Ives said they valued Nvidia at $300 per share with Huang as chief executive, compared with $225 without him, reflecting his central role in the company's strategy and its dominance in artificial intelligence chips.
Get premium analyst insights with InvestingPro -- at 55% off now
Nvidia was facing a rapidly evolving situation after The New York Times reported an alleged relationship between Huang and Kimberly Powell, the company's vice president of healthcare, while The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board was preparing to oust the CEO and could meet as soon as Wednesday to discuss his future.
Over the weekend, Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy.
"The writing is on the wall that Jensen's days at Nvidia could be numbered," analysts said, describing the next 48 hours as potentially volatile.
They said Huang was not replaceable by another chief executive or an interim management team, warning that uncertainty over his successor, Nvidia's strategic direction and potential board changes could weigh on the stock.
"Jensen has created a black eye moment for himself and Nvidia and now has created a spider web of complexity that Wall Street, Silicon Valley, DC, and the global tech ecosystem are trying to figure out what is next," analysts wrote.
However, Yorkville Ives said that Nvidia's entrenched position in the AI chip market and its leading GPU technology would remain intact despite the leadership turmoil, allowing the company to navigate the crisis and retain its central role in the AI industry.

title: Alaska judge rules against Democratic US ​Senate candidate’s request for absentee ballot data
full_text:
By Kanishka Singh
WASHINGTON, Nov 11 (Reuters) - A judge ruled on Wednesday that a request by the campaign of Democratic US Senate candidate Mary Peltola of Alaska seeking the immediate release of records identifying absentee ballots was not reasonable.
• Peltola’s campaign sued state election officials last week seeking the immediate release of records identifying absentee ballots that were rejected in the voting during this month’s US midterm elections
• Peltola and the Republican candidate, incumbent Senator Dan S. Sullivan, are in a tight race for the US Senate seat
• As of late Wednesday, US media tallies showed Peltola with a 1.6% lead with 86% of the votes counted
• If no candidate secures more than 50% of the vote, the race will head to a ranked-choice tabulation
• Superior Court Judge Thomas Matthews ruled that Alaska’s Division of Elections is "currently busy processing ballots from the 2026 general election" and "simply lacks the capacity to generate the report from" the voter registration database at the behest of Peltola’s campaign
• "Even if the request were otherwise considered reasonable outside the peak election time of year, it is simply not reasonable nor required right now," the ruling said
• Overall in the midterm elections, Democrats won a majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives, while President Donald Trump’s Republican Party suffered heavy losses in congressional and state races
• With Alaska still undecided, Democrats have a 55-44 Senate edge in the midterm tally
• An Alaska win would give Democrats 56 seats in the chamber

title: ASIC sues Commonwealth Bank over alleged customer overcharges
full_text:
Investing.com -- Australia’s corporate regulator filed civil penalty proceedings against Commonwealth Bank of Australia (ASX:CBA) on Thursday, alleging the lender overcharged business customers through fees that were not properly disclosed.
The Australian Securities and Investments Commission said about 42,000 CommBiz customers were overcharged approximately A$8.5 million ($5.82 million) in fees between November 2020 and May 31, 2025. CommBiz is the bank’s online banking platform for medium-to-large businesses.
ASIC said the platform’s terms and conditions failed to accurately disclose all fees charged for direct debit and direct credit transactions. The regulator said misleading terms had been in place since CommBiz launched in 2006, meaning business customers were overcharged for about 19 years.
The bank received customer complaints from at least 2015, and a 2016 internal audit identified the overcharging issues and recommended corrective action, ASIC said.
Commonwealth Bank temporarily stopped charging the relevant fees in June 2025, amended CommBiz terms in August 2025, and has waived the "contra leg" fees for processing direct debits and direct credits since February 2026, according to the regulator.
"What makes this particularly concerning is how long the alleged conduct went on, despite customer complaints to Commonwealth Bank pointing to a problem years earlier," ASIC Commissioner Alan Kirkland said.
Commonwealth Bank said it self-reported the matter and cooperated fully with ASIC’s investigation. The bank said it does not accept some of the allegations and expects to defend certain aspects of the claim while continuing to engage with the regulator.
The case marks the first major action under ASIC Chair Sarah Court, who took office on June 1.

title: Gold drops for a second straight session on boost to Fed rate hike expectations
full_text:
Investing.com -- Gold prices fell for a second straight session on Wednesday amid an extended surge in the dollar, as precious metal market participants continued to digest a rise in Federal Reserve rate hike expectations sparked by hot inflation data and hawkish commentary in the previous session.
Spot gold dropped 1.1% to settle at $3,987.93/oz, while gold futures fell 0.9% to settle at $3,994.30/oz. The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of six major peers, jumped 0.7% to 102.91.
Gold found support around $4,000 an ounce, thanks to central-bank purchases and strong physical demand in Asia, analysts at ING said in a note.
"While uncertainty over the Fed’s next move could keep prices volatile in the short term, underlying demand remains supportive," the analysts wrote.
Central banks are increasingly looking to gold as a strategic asset that allows them to "diversify their reserves and protect against both economic and geopolitical uncertainty," said Rick Kanda, Managing Director at The Gold Bullion Company.
On Tuesday, bullion retreated following a firmer-than-anticipated October U.S. consumer-price index report driven largely by stubbornly elevated energy costs.
Hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials added to the pressure on gold. Fed Governor Christopher Waller raised the possibility of a larger-than-normal 50-basis-point increase at the central bank’s December meeting, reinforcing concerns that policymakers may pursue more aggressive tightening to bring inflation under control. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan later said she believes rates need to eventually be raised by at least another 50 basis points.
The CPI data and the comments combined to solidify wagers that the central bank will lift rates at its upcoming policy meeting. Traders are now fully pricing in a 25-basis-point increase next month, while bets on a bigger half-point hike have also grown. The Fed previously raised rates for the first time in three years in September.
Short-dated Treasury yields climbed and a gauge of the dollar surged against this backdrop, putting pressure on gold. Higher borrowing costs tend to undermine non-interest-bearing gold by increasing the opportunity cost of holding the metal, while a stronger dollar makes bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies.
Roushni Nair and Anuron Mitra contributed to this article

The U.S. Dollar Index edged up 0.1% to 103.048 by 03:12 GMT, reaching its highest since early April 2025. The index rose 0.7% in the previous session.

Yen nears 160, raising intervention risks

The Chinese yuan's onshore USD/CNY and offshore USD/CNH pairs traded largely flat.
The South Korean won's USD/KRW pair, meanwhile, fell 0.5%.

title: BHP names Adrian Wood as new chief financial officer
full_text:
Investing.com -- BHP (ASX:BHP) announced Thursday that Adrian Wood will become its new chief financial officer, replacing Vandita Pant in the latest senior management change since the mining company’s new chief executive took office in July.
Wood joined the world’s largest listed mining company in 2015 and currently serves as vice president projects for its Minerals Australia business. He brings more than 25 years of experience from investment banking and corporate roles in Australia and Britain, including positions at UBS in London and Macquarie Group.
"Adrian has a strong track record of financial management, strategic thinking and commercial capability," BHP CEO Brandon Craig said in a statement.
Pant will step down after BHP releases its half-year results on February 16 and will remain with the company until March 29 to support the transition.
Pant is the second top executive who had been viewed as a potential CEO candidate to leave since Craig assumed the top role. BHP announced in September that Chief Commercial Officer Rag Udd would step down at the end of January to pursue an opportunity outside the company.
Craig took over this year as the mining industry undergoes changes amid increased demand for copper. He succeeded Mike Henry, who served six years in the role.
CEO transitions typically lead to around a third of top management departing within a few years, a pattern BHP Chairman Ross McEwan in March described as a natural outcome of competitive succession processes.

title: Indonesian rupiah hits record low amid MSCI downgrade concerns
full_text:
Investing.com-- The Indonesian rupiah dropped to a record low on Thursday as the dollar strengthened and concerns grew over potential exclusion from MSCI Inc. emerging-market indexes.
The rupiah’s USD/IDR pair-- which measures the amount of rupiah needed to buy one dollar-- as much as 0.5% to a record high of 18,242.4 per dollar, surpassing its previous record of 18,190 reached in early June.
MSCI announced Wednesday it will remove two Indonesian companies-- Barito Pacific and Bumi Resources Minerals-- from its global index, effective November 30.
The decision follows an October warning from the global index provider that Indonesian stocks could face removal from its indexes next year, potentially relegating the market to "frontier" market status.
The rupiah has become Asia’s worst-performing currency this year. The benchmark Jakarta Composite Index has fallen over 40% in 2026, making it the world’s worst-performing major stock market.
The drop was fueled chiefly by an exodus of foreign investors.
While Jakarta has raced to meet the MSCI’s calls for more market reforms, investors have questioned whether the government will be able to overhaul local markets in time.

title: Senior US Democratic senators urge administration to preserve Nvidia export records amid China security concerns
full_text:
Nov 11 (Reuters) - Senior US Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked the Trump administration to preserve all documents tied to Nvidia’s chip exports to China, amid growing scrutiny over CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.
Nvidia’s board is meeting late on Wednesday to decide whether to oust Huang, a person familiar with the matter said, after media reports alleged he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing.
"This incident raises significant concerns about the federal government’s ability to effectively enforce our export controls and protect our national security,” the senators said in the letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller.
The controversy escalated on several fronts this week as allegations emerged that Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang aided at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to China and that Rubio had previously briefed President Donald Trump on the affair. Many of Nvidia’s most advanced chips are subject to US export restrictions to protect the country’s dominance in the critical sector.
"Questions also remain regarding whether or not prudent defensive counter-intelligence action was taken or national security recommendations were overruled," the senators said.
Warren and Coons also requested a congressional briefing on the national security risks posed by the suspected intelligence operation.
The Wall Street Journal first reported details of the letter.

title: Technoprobe shares fall over 5% as lower revenue outlook misses analyst consensus
full_text:
Investing.com -- Technoprobe shares fell on Thursday after the semiconductor testing equipment maker lowered its full-year revenue outlook below analyst expectations, overshadowing strong nine-month growth driven by demand for artificial intelligence and data centre infrastructure.
Shares dropped 5.4% to €22.42, giving back some of the previous session’s gains, when they surged 7.7%. The FTSE MIB was little changed during the session.
Technoprobe reported revenue of €787.4 million for the first nine months of 2026, up 68.8% from a year earlier. EBITDA more than doubled to €376.3 million from €146.1 million, while the EBITDA margin reached 47.8%, supported by higher volumes, a favourable product mix and operating leverage.
Third-quarter revenue came in 3% above company guidance, according to Goldman Sachs, reflecting continued volume growth and higher testing intensity in AI-related applications, alongside a modest recovery in consumer and automotive and industrial markets. Gross margin was 61.2%, slightly below the 61.5% guidance, while EBITDA margin reached 52.6%.
The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of approximately €270 million, implying full-year 2026 revenue of €1.05 billion to €1.065 billion, below Visible Alpha consensus of €1.1 billion ahead of the results.
Technoprobe said the outlook reflects the ramp-up of manufacturing capacity and investments ahead of stronger demand. It plans to reach annual installed manufacturing capacity of approximately €2 billion by the end of 2027.
Goldman Sachs reiterated its Buy rating, saying robust AI demand, rising testing intensity and the expanding high-bandwidth memory opportunity underpin long-term growth. The broker also highlighted temporary margin pressure from headcount expansion ahead of the 2027 capacity ramp, but said the company’s manufacturing expansion supports its longer-term opportunity.
Sam Boughedda contributed to this article.

title: European shares hit record highs as defensive appeal offsets Nvidia shock
full_text:
Investing.com - European shares edged higher on Thursday, striking a fresh record high, as robust corporate earnings and the region’s defensive composition offset volatility in technology stocks triggered by mounting leadership turmoil at AI-bellwether Nvidia.
The pan-European STOXX 600 index rose 0.4%, bringing the gauge to an all-time peak.
Germany’s DAX rose 1.1%, France’s CAC 40 was up 0.6% and London’s FTSE 100 was up 0.3%. 
The advance extends a durable autumn rally anchored by a highly constructive third-quarter earnings season.
With corporate scorecards continuing to print better-than-expected results, investors have been reassured that European balance sheets remain fundamentally healthy despite months of acute volatility across global bond and energy markets.
Crucially, Europe’s traditional "value-oriented" index composition - lacking the heavy concentration of mega-cap technology and artificial intelligence stocks that dominate Wall Street - the STOXX 600 has been largely insulated from the violent rotational swings currently whipping through the global AI trade from New York to Tokyo to Seoul.
However, overall index gains were kept on a tight leash as localized technology shares grappled with severe cross-border headwinds emanating from Silicon Valley.
European semiconductor and enterprise software stocks, which had enjoyed a robust relief rally in the previous session, turned largely lower on Thursday.
The sector-wide retreat tracked a steep 7.4% drop in Frankfurt-listed shares of Nvidia, as global markets digested the growing prospect that Chief Executive Jensen Huang could be ousted from the company.
The unprecedented corporate governance crisis at the vanguard of the artificial intelligence boom has severely rattled global risk appetite.
Markets pivot to UK GDP and Eurozone forecasts
Traders are bracing for the release of the UK’s third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) figures, which will provide a definitive scorecard on how the British economy is absorbing the Bank of England’s current interest-rate environment.
Simultaneously, financial markets are awaiting updated economic forecasts from the Eurozone.
The regional growth and inflation projections will be heavily scrutinized for clues regarding the European Central Bank’s policy trajectory heading into 2027. If the forecasts confirm that the bloc is successfully avoiding a formal recession while inflation continues to cool, the STOXX 600 may find the fundamental runway needed to finally clear its record-high threshold.
Meanwhile, sentiment among European companies has picked up since June, but there are growing concerns about rising inflation and sovereign debt, according to a survey published by BusinessEurope.

title: China chip stocks rally as U.S. weighs curbs on remote AI access
full_text:
Investing.com -- Chinese chip stocks rallied on Thursday, with Cambricon surging more than 11% and Moore Threads gaining around 7%, as a rebound in global semiconductor shares and the prospect of tighter U.S. controls on access to advanced AI processors renewed focus on China's domestic chip industry.
SMIC's Shanghai-listed shares rose 2.42%, while its Hong Kong-listed stock added 1.67%. Hua Hong Semiconductor gained 2.7% and chip equipment maker NAURA Technology advanced 3.12%.
The gains contrasted with weakness among several Chinese technology companies, with Z.AI falling 7.4%, MiniMax dropping 6.1% and Alibaba declining 4.9%.
The sector's advance followed a strong rally in U.S. semiconductor shares on Wednesday, when the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index climbed 5.7%.
Strong results from AI cloud provider CoreWeave helped ease concerns about the financing and sustainability of data-centre investment, supporting demand for chipmakers and other AI infrastructure suppliers. Chinese financial media also highlighted the overnight rebound as a driver of gains in domestic semiconductor stocks.
Investors were also assessing a potential tightening of U.S. restrictions. The Information reported that the Commerce Department was preparing a rule to prevent Chinese AI companies from remotely accessing advanced chips through data centres in other countries.
The measure could be announced as soon as this month and extend existing semiconductor-related controls to seven additional countries, including Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand. The proposal remains under interagency review and has not been finalised.
The proposed restrictions would target a route through which Chinese companies can obtain computing capacity without physically importing restricted processors. Tencent, Alibaba and ByteDance have signed agreements with overseas data-centre operators that provide access to advanced Nvidia chips for AI training, according to The Information.
The prospect of tighter controls could reinforce Beijing's push to develop domestic alternatives and reduce reliance on foreign technology. However, the shift is not automatic: Chinese chipmakers continue to face constraints in advanced manufacturing and other parts of the semiconductor supply chain.

title: Gold slips below $4,000 as hawkish Fed bets keep bullion under pressure
full_text:
Investing.com -- Gold prices prices fell below $4,000 an ounce on Thursday, extending losses from the previous session as persistent inflation concerns and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary reinforced expectations of another interest-rate increase in December.
At 00:16 ET (05:16 GMT), spot gold fell 0.4% to $3,973.13 an ounce, while U.S. gold futures declined 0.6% to $3,978.57.

title: Bitcoin slips to $73.6k; Strategy drops on MSCI index removal
full_text:
Investing.com-- Bitcoin fell on Thursday as sentiment towards cryptocurrencies remained quashed by risks from higher U.S. interest rates and a less favorable regulatory outlook.
Strategy was a new point of concern, after index operator MSCI said the stock will be removed from several of its benchmarks– a scenario that heralds tighter capital conditions for the stock.

Crypto markets struggled to make headway after falling sharply through October and early-November, amid a number of growing risks for the sector.
Hot U.S. inflation data saw markets dial up expectations for more interest rate hikes by the Fed, which could come as soon as December. Higher rates diminish the appeal of non-yielding, risk-heavy assets like crypto.
On the regulatory front, the Democrat sweep of the U.S. midterm elections sparked concerns over greater Congressional scrutiny towards crypto.
Strategy shares fall as MSCI confirms index exit
Strategy Inc (NASDAQ:MSTR) shares fell 4% in aftermarket trade on Wednesday after MSCI confirmed the stock will be removed from its global indexes after determining they more closely operate akin to investment funds.
The index operator had last year proposed to remove digital asset treasury companies, whose holdings represent over 50% of their total assets, amid a broader review into what it deemed as “non-operating companies.”
Japan’s Metaplanet Inc (TYO:3350), which is the world’s second-largest Bitcoin treasury by coins held, was also slated to be removed from MSCI indexes.
Strategy had warned earlier that an MSCI exclusion would result in $2.8 billion of its stock being liquidated, and would also hurt the broader crypto industry.
The company has fueled its Bitcoin purchases chiefly through massive debt and capital issuances, leaving it vulnerable to any pullback. Strategy had sold some of its Bitcoin holdings earlier this year to meet mounting debt obligations.
The recurrence of such a scenario presents more selling pressure for Bitcoin.

title: Alphabet’s debut Hong Kong, Singapore bond sales draw over $7 billion in orders
full_text:
By Yantoultra Ngui and Nikita Maria Jino
Nov 12 (Reuters) - Google parent Alphabet’s first Hong Kong and Singapore dollar bond sales drew combined orders of more than $7 billion Thursday, including orders from banks arranging the deals, according to updated deal statistics seen by Reuters.
Alphabet was considering minimum sizes of HK$8 billion for the Hong Kong dollar portion and S$1.5 billion for the Singapore dollar portion, Reuters reported on Wednesday.
The strong order books give Alphabet flexibility to increase its planned financing as it accelerates investment in AI infrastructure, even as recent volatility in technology shares has made investors more selective.
Orders for the three-part Hong Kong dollar offering exceeded HK$32.5 billion ($4.1 billion), up from more than HK$24 billion earlier in the day. The book includes HK$13.23 billion from joint lead managers.
Orders for the four-part Singapore dollar offering exceeded S$4 billion ($3.1 billion), including S$965 million of interest from joint lead managers, up from more than S$2.5 billion earlier in the day.
Alphabet set final price guidance for its Hong Kong dollar tranches at 4.35% for the 2028 tranche, 4.70% for the 2031 tranche and 5.20% for the 2036 tranche. The final levels were tighter than initial guidance of 4.60%, 5.00% and 5.50%, respectively.
It set final price guidance for its Singapore dollar tranches at 2.50% for the 2028 tranche, 3.00% for the 2031 tranche, 3.40% for the 2036 tranche and 3.80% for the 2056 tranche. The final levels were tighter than initial guidance of 2.75%, 3.25%, 3.65% and 4.00%, respectively.
HSBC and JPMorgan are joint global coordinators. For the Hong Kong dollar bonds, Bank of China (Hong Kong), ICBC, and Standard Chartered are arranging the sale. DBS, OCBC, and United Overseas Bank will arrange the Singapore dollar bond sale.
The bonds, which are due to settle on November 19 and are expected to be rated Aa2 by Moody’s and AA+ by S&P, would help expand and diversify Alphabet’s geographic debt footprint.
Alphabet last week raised €6 billion ($6.7 billion) through a euro-denominated bond sale. It also sold $25 billion of US dollar bonds in August and A$5.5 billion ($3.8 billion) of Australian dollar bonds in the same month.

title: B&M shares surge 16% as H1 profit outlook beats expectations, UK sales rebound
full_text:

Chief Executive Tjeerd Jegen said the company’s strategy was starting to deliver, with improved on-shelf availability and revamped promotions.

title: Siemens shares hit 11-week high after earnings beat, outlook upgrade
full_text:
Investing.com -- Siemens AG (ETR:SIEGn) shares climbed to an 11-week high on Thursday after the industrial group reported better-than-expected quarterly results and raised its medium-term growth targets, as strong demand for AI-related data centre equipment and rail contracts drove record orders.
Shares rose 4.44% to €289.30, after touching an intraday high of €291.45, their highest level since August 28. The stock outperformed Germany’s benchmark DAX, which gained around 0.9% during the session.
Net income for the quarter ended September 30 rose to €2.43 billion from €1.84 billion a year earlier. Revenue increased 11% to €23.68 billion, while profit at its Industrial Business climbed 22% to a record €3.90 billion. The industrial profit margin improved to 16.8% from 15.3%.
Orders surged 58% to a quarterly record €34.77 billion, lifting Siemens’ book-to-bill ratio to 1.47 and its order backlog to €143 billion.
Growth was led by Smart Infrastructure and Mobility, reflecting sustained investment in electrification, digital infrastructure and rail transportation. Smart Infrastructure’s revenue rose 16% to €7.24 billion, with order intake jumping 40%, supported by large data centre contract wins, particularly in the U.S. and Europe.
Digital Industries also delivered stronger results, with revenue up 11% and profit increasing 50%, driven primarily by operational improvements in automation. Mobility’s orders more than quadrupled, supported by major German rail contracts, including a €2.4 billion high-speed train order.
Looking ahead, Siemens expects comparable revenue growth of 9% to 11% in fiscal 2027 and earnings per share before purchase price allocation accounting (EPS pre PPA) of €10.20 to €10.80. The company cited continued investment in AI and digital infrastructure, public investment programmes and a recovery in industrial activity as key growth drivers.
For the full fiscal year, net income declined 9% to €9.47 billion, reflecting a €2.1 billion gain from the sale of Innomotics included in the previous year’s results. Revenue rose 6% to €83.37 billion, while Industrial Business profit increased 13% to a record €13.29 billion. Siemens proposed increasing its dividend to €5.50 per share from €5.35.

The broker also highlighted scope for further margin expansion in Gas Services and Grid Technologies, with its long-term outlook supported by rising turbine demand and service revenue growth.

title: Poste Italiane Q3 profit beats forecasts on insurance, payments growth
full_text:
Investing.com -- Poste Italiane beat third-quarter profit forecasts on Thursday, driven by growth in insurance and payments, but maintained its 2026 standalone targets, as it prepares to integrate newly acquired Telecom Italia (TIM).
The Italian postal, financial and insurance group reported adjusted operating profit of €910 million, up 6.3% year on year, against a company-compiled analyst consensus of €866 million.
Adjusted net profit, excluding its stake in TIM, rose 4.2% to €629 million, compared with consensus of €598 million.
Revenue increased 4.5% to €3.32 billion, in line with consensus.
Insurance adjusted operating profit rose 12% to €429 million, beating consensus of €416 million.
Revenue increased 13% to €504 million, reflecting higher releases in life insurance and an improved combined ratio in protection. Gross written premiums fell 8.2% to €4.71 billion.
Postepay Services, which covers payments, telecoms and energy, reported adjusted operating profit of €164 million, up 16.7% and above consensus of €150 million, driven by strong revenue growth and cost efficiencies. Revenue rose 6.4% to €435 million.
Mail, parcel and distribution adjusted operating profit fell 31.3% to €48 million from €70 million a year earlier, against consensus of €25 million.
Mail revenue declined 4% to €461 million, while mail volumes fell 11.5% to 396 million items. Parcel volumes increased 0.1% to 87 million, although they rose 11% excluding China, where volumes were affected by recent EU duties.
Financial services adjusted operating profit rose 2.6% to €269 million, below consensus of €275 million. Postal savings recorded net outflows of €571 million in the quarter, compared with net inflows of €873 million a year earlier.
Poste confirmed its 2026 standalone targets of €3.4 billion in adjusted operating profit and €2.3 billion in adjusted net profit, which exclude TIM’s fourth-quarter contribution.
In the first nine months, adjusted operating profit rose 6.6% to €2.68 billion, while adjusted net profit increased 3.8% to €1.84 billion.
Poste consolidated TIM’s balance sheet on Sept. 30 and will include its profit and loss from Oct. 1. TIM had net debt of €10.28 billion, or €7.13 billion excluding lease obligations, while pro forma leverage was below 1.5 times. Poste holds 86.952% of TIM after completing its takeover and exchange offer.
The board approved an interim dividend of €0.43 per share, up 7.5%, payable on Nov. 25, with an ex-dividend date of Nov. 23.
The total payout will rise 32% to €686 million, reflecting the higher share count following the TIM offer.

title: Hapag-Lloyd raises 2026 outlook again, says Q4 developing better than expected
full_text:
Investing.com -- Hapag-Lloyd on Thursday raised its 2026 earnings outlook for the second time, saying fourth-quarter business is developing better than expected on continued robust spot freight rates.
The German container shipper now expects group EBITDA of $4.6 billion to $5.0 billion (€4.0 billion to €4.4 billion) and group EBIT of $2.0 billion to $2.4 billion (€1.7 billion to €2.1 billion). This compares with previous expectations of $3.9 billion to $4.4 billion and $1.25 billion to $1.75 billion, respectively.
The group said the outlook is subject to a considerable degree of uncertainty given volatile freight rates and persistent geopolitical challenges.
For the third quarter, Hapag-Lloyd EBITDA nearly doubled to $1.73 billion from $866 million a year earlier, and the EBITDA margin widened to 25.1% from 15.9%. EBIT rose to $1.09 billion from $228 million, and group profit rose to $999 million from $172 million.
Revenue rose to $6.88 billion from $5.46 billion.
The shipper credited much higher freight rates, strong vessel use and growth in its terminals business. The average freight rate was $1,808 per container unit, up from $1,413. Volumes were flat at 3.4 million containers, despite the conflict in the Middle East and weather disruptions, which also pushed up unit costs.
Terminal and Infrastructure revenue rose to $197 million from $131 million, and EBIT rose to $34 million from $9 million, helped by new capacity and better performance at Latin American terminals.
Despite the strong quarter, nine-month group profit was $827 million, down from $946 million a year earlier. EBIT for the nine months rose to $1.10 billion from $905 million.
"We delivered a strong third quarter, driven by significantly higher spot rates, robust demand and high capacity utilization," Chief Executive Rolf Habben Jansen said. He added that unit costs remain under pressure from geopolitical tensions and disruptions.

full_text:

The guidance compares with a consensus of about £2.3 billion, according to Jefferies.
The British defense contractor left its guidance for sales, earnings before interest and tax and earnings per share unchanged from the upgrade it gave with first-half results in July.

Orders so far this year total £33 billion, and the company expects more agreements before year-end. Second-half awards include about £4.3 billion of funding for the U.K.’s Dreadnought nuclear submarines, about £1.6 billion for the Global Combat Air Programme and about £1.5 billion from MBDA-related work.
They also include about A$1.3 billion for an Australian over-the-horizon radar system in Canada, which BAE called Australia’s largest-ever defense export. U.S. awards include about $1.0 billion for munitions programs, $0.8 billion for armored vehicles and $0.5 billion for Army ammunition plants.
BAE said strong trading in its Electronic Systems, Air and Platforms & Services divisions more than offset subdued growth and margins in Maritime, where it is in the first-in-class stage of the Type 26 frigate program. In the U.S., it said its portfolio is strongly aligned with government priorities, and it supports 10 of the 12 munitions programs picked for increased production capacity.
Jefferies analysts said the update "reinforces our view that meaningful margin recovery" in Maritime "will take time," though they called the strength in Electronic Systems "reassuring."
BAE expects to return about £1.6 billion to shareholders in 2026, including about £500 million of share buybacks. It will report full-year results on Feb. 19, 2027.

title: UK Q3 GDP rises 0.7% as business services offset construction slump
full_text:
Investing.com -- Britain’s economy grew by 0.7% in the third quarter, matching forecasts, as business services, including AI-related computing work, offset contractions in construction and hospitality, official data showed on Thursday.
Growth accelerated from 0.5% in the April-June quarter. Output was 1.9% higher than a year earlier, also in line with forecasts, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said.
Monthly data showed output rose 0.2% in September, beating forecasts of no growth. August was revised down to no growth from 0.1%, while July’s 0.4% growth was unchanged.
Services output rose 0.9%, with business-facing services increasing 1% and consumer-facing services up 0.5%.
Administrative and support services grew 4.1%, driven by a 6.6% rise in rental and leasing. Information and communication output increased 2.1%, with computer programming and consultancy up 4.4%.
The ONS said information and communication had been the largest driver of growth in 2026, with many businesses reporting the biggest increases in turnover involved in artificial intelligence and cloud computing.
Construction output fell 0.7%, with private housing new work down 4.7%. Accommodation and food services declined 0.5%, driven by a 1.9% fall in food and beverage services. Production output rose 0.1%.
Household spending increased 0.6%, while fixed investment rose 1.7%. Business investment grew 0.4%.
Exports rose 1.6% and imports increased 1.8%. The GDP deflator, a measure of prices across the economy, rose 2.3% from a year earlier.

title: 3i Group shares hit 10-week high after £750 million buyback announcement
full_text:
Investing.com -- 3i Group PLC shares climbed to a 10-week high on Thursday after the investment firm announced a fresh share buyback programme alongside its half-year results, even as foreign-exchange losses and lower investment gains weighed on its portfolio returns.
Shares rose 3.65% to 2,658.60 pence, their highest level since August 31, outperforming the broader FTSE 100, which was up around 0.2% during the session.
Profit for the six months to September 30 fell 51% to £1.619 billion from £3.291 billion a year earlier. Total return on opening shareholders’ funds dropped to 5% from 13%, while gross investment return declined to £1.722 billion from £3.406 billion.
The period included a £474 million foreign-exchange translation loss, compared with a £771 million gain a year earlier.
Private equity generated £1.515 billion in gross investment returns, down from £3.234 billion; Action accounted for £1.337 billion. Operating cash profit was £259 million, compared with a £12 million loss a year earlier, as portfolio cash income rose, mainly due to the timing of Action’s second dividend, and operating expenses fell.
Action’s net sales rose 14% to €12.761 billion and operating EBITDA increased 11% to €1.730 billion in the nine reporting periods through September 27. In the ten periods through October 25, sales and EBITDA were up 14% and 12%, respectively.
Like-for-like sales growth reached 3.7% through November 8, supported by more than 1,000 price reductions and the addition of 286 net new stores.
3i expects Action to deliver full-year like-for-like sales growth of about 4% and an EBITDA margin of 14.7%-14.8%, while opening at least 400 stores in 2026.
3i said it would end its existing £750 million buyback, having purchased about 29.5 million shares for roughly £742 million by November 11, and launch a second programme of up to £750 million to be completed by the end of May 2027.
The company also proposed a 42.25-pence first dividend for FY2027, payable in January.
